title: Timothy's method: counterpoint and the three progressions
summary: Thomas credits Timothy, a Schillinger pupil, for teaching counterpoint in six weeks and a mathematical view of progressions and the cycle of fifths.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: All right. And he just opened a whole world to me. Because see, Timothy had studied with your teacher...
And I didn't have the privilege of studying with Schillinger. I guess I wasn't ready to study with Schillinger anyway, when he was in town. But I studied from
Timothy, who I think was one of his good pupils. But Timothy had studied counterpoint from some great teacher. I don't know his name. He taught me counterpoint in six weeks. And I had...
So Timothy showed you the influence of Christian Science in music.

Yeah. And Timothy's method in music was mathematical. For one instance, there's only three progressions in music, the Second, Third and Fifth. And there's a minor second and a minor third and a diminished fifth. But that's it. There's no more progressions in music. You can figure it out. I figured it out mathematically. And it turned out to be... And it made it so easy! Now, the principle of it, the third up is the same as a third down. It's still a third. That's where that Math comes back. I could talk for days on this.

And the one progression that goes through all...the whole chromatic scale is the progression of the fifth up. I guess it goes in with fifth down. But fifth up. You keep going to a fifth up, a fifth up, a fifth up; when you get through to end up that first note you started on, you will go through the whole chromatic scale.
So that's those fifths up you're talking about, going through the whole chromatic...
